author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow both veterinarian list surfaces to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces - the paged page and the machine-readable document - accept an optional specialty name and list only veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive. A blank value lists everyone; a specialty nobody holds lists no one without failing. Paging keeps the specialty in force. No page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: Both /vets.html and /vets accept an optional query parameter named specialty; no other request shape carries the filter.
Given /vets.html?specialty=<name> where some veterinarians hold that specialty, only those veterinarians are listed, and paging applies to the narrowed list.
Given /vets?specialty=<name>, the machine-readable document carries only those veterinarians.
Matching is on the whole specialty name, ignoring letter case: radiology, Radiology, and RADIOLOGY all match the seeded radiology specialty.
Matching is not prefix matching: radio matches no veterinarian even though radiology exists.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, the page renders normally with an empty veterinarian list and succeeds (HTTP 200); the machine-readable document carries no veterinarians and succeeds.
Given specialty= or a value of only spaces, both surfaces behave as if the parameter were absent and list every veterinarian, as an empty owner search does (REQ-OWN-002 precedent).
Given no specialty parameter, both surfaces behave exactly as today.
Pagination links on the narrowed page carry the specialty parameter, so following a page link keeps the narrowing in force.
A veterinarian holding several specialties is listed whenever any one of them is named.
No form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the specialty is added to any template (NG-10).
Case-insensitive matching holds on every supported database vendor, not only where the collation happens to ignore case.
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the specialty - NG-10, deferred to its own request
free-text veterinarian search - NG-9 stands, narrowed only to admit this attribute filter
paging the machine-readable list
naming more than one specialty in one request
notes: ADR obligation for the design triage: author docs/adr/2026-08-11-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md capturing (1) the owner's 2026-08-11 narrowing of NG-9 - free-text veterinarian search out, narrowing the directory by an already-displayed attribute in; (2) the machine-readable /vets surface reinstated as supported under the fresh REQ-VET-004, with REQ-VET-002 staying withdrawn and its id never reused; (3) NG-10 - the filter is a request-level contract only, a visible control deferred to a later request. Once the ADR exists, the NG-9 rationale cell's 'Non-goal ADR pending in this slice' must become a link to it, and the REQ-VET-002 Superseded entry may cite it. My write scope covers docs/adr/*-non-goal-*.md, but this dispatch reserved ADR authorship for the design triage, so I left the file unwritten rather than dangle a link. Narrowest readings taken where the request was silent, recorded in PRD Open Questions rather than blocking: one specialty per request; the machine-readable document stays unpaged; a value with surrounding spaces is matched as given, so it matches nothing - deliberately not pinned by an acceptance bullet, so it can settle either way. Vendor caution: owner search's case-insensitive rule is defeated under PostgreSQL (Owner records edge case 3) because it leans on the stored column's case handling; the specialty match must not repeat that. Contracts to update in system-design.md: VetController and VetRepository rows gain REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, and the Vets wrapper stops being a contract that serves no requirement.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter is the vet package's first narrowed read, and it settles three project-level rules that no durable memory carried: predicate placement, vendor-uniform case folding, and cache policy for a caller-keyed read. All three are now recorded in docs/system-design.md § Veterinarian list reads with back-links to the new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-11-vet-specialty-filter-read-path.md. Structurally the slice stays inside the existing shape: one feature package, controller reading a Spring Data repository directly, no new package, no new dependency, no change to the acyclic package graph. DECISION 1, where the filter belongs: in VetRepository as a derived-query predicate returning Page<Vet>, following the OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith precedent. Filtering the cached collection in the controller is rejected on two counts - architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog bars a new rule in a web controller ('A new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing one', line 91, checklist line 144), and hand-rolled paging would compute totalPages and totalItems in Java where the store already computes them. DECISION 2, case-insensitive whole-name matching: the trap does apply here, and worse than for owner search. specialties.name is VARCHAR(80) under H2 and TEXT under PostgreSQL (both case-sensitive) and case-insensitive only under MySQL's default collation - unlike owners.last_name, which H2 declares VARCHAR_IGNORECASE and so masks the PostgreSQL defect from the default test suite. The implementer must therefore put the case folding in the generated query, not lean on the column: the Spring Data IgnoreCase keyword on the nested property (a name of the findDistinctBySpecialties...NameIgnoreCase shape) emits upper()/lower() in the SQL and is uniform on all three vendors; an explicit @Query with lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty) is equally acceptable. Distinct is wanted: no vendor schema declares specialties.name unique, so two rows differing only in case would otherwise duplicate a vet. DECISION 3, the two surfaces sharing one filter: one repository predicate serves both. /vets.html passes the PageRequest it builds today; /vets passes Pageable.unpaged() (a second unpaged overload of the same derived name is acceptable if unpaged() misbehaves, but the predicate stays derived from one name, never hand-written twice). Normalization exists once too: one private helper in VetController strips the value and treats blank as absent, exactly as OwnerController does for lastName. Normalizing a bound request value is request adaptation, not a business rule, so it stays in the controller without breaching the Web controller row.
integration_points: VetRepository gains one specialty predicate returning Page<Vet>; the two existing findAll methods and their @Cacheable("vets") annotations are untouched, which is what makes 'without the parameter, behaves exactly as today' hold by construction

VetController's two handlers each gain an optional specialty @RequestParam and share one private normalization helper; the filtered branch calls the new predicate, the unfiltered branch keeps calling findAll
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty; the model gains a specialty attribute so the links can render it
ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest against H2 with the seeded radiology/surgery/dentistry rows) is where the case-folding and whole-name behavior is actually exercised against SQL

patterns.description: repository-level derived predicate returning Page<T> with Pageable - the precedent for predicate placement; note it omits IgnoreCase, which is the half not to copy
request-value normalization in the controller: null to empty, strip(), broadest-search semantics for a blank term - the precedent for the blank-means-absent rule
existing findPaginated helper and its local pageSize - the filtered path reuses this page shape rather than introducing a second one
the three rules this slice puts in force, each back-linked to the ADR

risks.risk: Case-insensitivity is asserted only through VetControllerTests, where @MockitoBean VetRepository makes any stubbed answer pass. The acceptance criterion about every vendor would then be untested - the exact mechanism by which the PostgreSQL owner-search defect stayed invisible.
risks.mitigation: Cover the matching semantics (whole-name, mixed case, prefix non-match, no-match empty) in ClinicServiceTests against real SQL. H2 stores specialties.name case-sensitively, so a mixed-case assertion there fails if the folding is left to the collation.

risks.risk: Caching the filtered read would make an arbitrary caller-supplied string a cache key in a cache with no eviction and no size bound (CacheConfiguration builds a bare MutableConfiguration; no caffeine spec or expiry is configured). Unbounded memory growth from an unauthenticated GET - every route here is open.
risks.mitigation: Do not annotate the new predicate @Cacheable. Recorded as a rule in system-design.md § Veterinarian list reads and as rejected option 4 in the ADR.

risks.risk: Concatenating the user-supplied specialty into the pagination href, copying the existing '/vets.html?page=__${i}__' preprocessing style, puts unescaped request input into a URL and re-enters Thymeleaf preprocessing.
risks.mitigation: Render the links with link-expression parameters - @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} - so Thymeleaf URL-encodes the value. Never inside a preprocessed string literal.

risks.risk: A Page over a ManyToMany join can surprise: duplicate rows without Distinct, and the count query must count distinct vets for totalPages to be right.
risks.mitigation: Use the Distinct keyword in the derived name; assert totalPages and totalItems against a narrowed list in the tests, not only the row count on page one.

risks.risk: Pagination-link rendering can trip on a null model value if the parameter is absent.
risks.mitigation: Always place a specialty model attribute (normalized value or empty string) and always render it on the links. Criterion 7 defines specialty= as equivalent to absent, so an empty rendered parameter is behaviorally correct and needs no conditional.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, skipped. OBLIGATIONS DISCHARGED: (1) the false Known Defects row 'The machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' is deleted - no other doc referenced it, and the section preamble still reads true; (2) the VetController and VetRepository contract rows now carry REQ-VET-001, REQ-VET-003, REQ-VET-004, and Vets carries REQ-VET-004, which also repairs the Contracts preamble's claim that only three kinds of contract show an em dash; (3) docs/adr/README.md's index gained rows for both 2026-08-11 ADRs - the non-goal one and mine. Also touched: the provenance blockquote gained one clause admitting post-survey decided statements, since the global 'read off the working tree' claim no longer covers the new section; and Open Question 5 now records that the vets cache has no size bound either. PRD OPEN QUESTION SETTLED, no requirement change needed: the design takes strip() over match-as-given, so ' radiology ' matches. The PRD left that unpinned by any acceptance bullet precisely so the design could settle it; the whitespace-only rule then falls out of the same strip() rather than needing a second check. product-requirements-expert may close that Open Questions entry citing the ADR - I did not touch prd.md. No conflict found with any acceptance criterion, so no consultation-request was raised. OBSERVATION, out of scope, do not copy: owner pagination links ('/owners?page=N') drop the lastName term, so owner search paging silently widens to all owners past page one. That is a latent defect of the same family as this slice's criterion 9, unrecorded in Known Defects and belonging to REQ-OWN-002, not here. Flagging it for the PRD expert's next owner slice. DOCTOR: the one failure, 'project-data: spec_version 0.1.0 does not match manifest 0.2.0', is unchanged by this dispatch (61 checks, that one failure). It should not become a PRD slice - it is harness-runtime metadata, not product behavior, so no requirement can carry it. Fix it as a chore commit with the next harness upgrade; leaving it red risks masking a real doctor failure on a later slice.

approved_aspects: Reflected-input risk closed: every pagination href in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html now uses a Thymeleaf link expression with a parameter list (@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}); the pre-existing '?page=__${i}__' preprocessing form is gone from this file, so no request-supplied text reaches Thymeleaf expression preprocessing. Link-expression parameters are URL-encoded and the th:href attribute value is HTML-escaped, and VetControllerTests#theVetListPaginationShouldEncodeTheSpecialtyItKeeps witnesses both (specialty=cardio%20%26%20vascular, and & separators rendered as &). Full read of vetList.html confirms the specialty model attribute reaches no other sink: it appears only inside the five link expressions, never in th:utext, th:attr, inline JavaScript, or a raw text node.

Cache-poisoning risk closed: findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase in VetRepository carries @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable, with an inline comment recording why. CacheConfiguration still builds a bare MutableConfiguration (statistics only, no expiry, no size bound), so no caller-supplied specialty ever becomes a key in the unbounded vets cache, as the read-path ADR requires. The unfiltered path is unchanged: findAll() keys on SimpleKey.EMPTY and findAll(Pageable) keys on the Pageable, distinct key spaces in the same cache, so the new predicate introduces no key collision and no new retained state.

Injection risk closed: the predicate is a Spring Data derived query, so both the specialty value and the case folding are structural (bound parameter plus a generated upper() comparison). Swept src/main/java for string-built queries: the only @Query in the codebase is PetTypeRepository's static ORDER BY with no parameters, and there is no createQuery, createNativeQuery, nativeQuery, or EntityManager use anywhere. No shell execution, no reflection, no deserialization surface is touched by the diff.

Hostile-value handling degrades to an empty result only. normalizeSpecialty strips and treats blank as no filter; a long or unusual-Unicode value travels as a bound JDBC parameter compared against specialties.name, so an over-length or non-matching value yields zero rows rather than an error, and the query string itself is bounded by the container's request-line limit before reaching the controller. Case folding runs in the query (upper()), so the worst locale-folding edge case is a miss, not a failure. Interaction with the existing page parameter is clean: the parameters bind independently, the JSON route ignores page entirely, and the pre-existing typed-binding and PageRequest bounds behavior is unchanged. Even on the pre-existing error-page defect the specialty value is not an XSS vector: error.html renders the message with th:text (escaped), and the IllegalArgumentException text carries no request string.

title: Narrow both veterinarian list surfaces to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces - the paged page and the machine-readable document - accept an optional specialty name and list only veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive, and ignores spaces around the name. A blank value lists everyone; a specialty nobody holds lists no one without failing. Paging keeps the specialty in force.
acceptance_criteria: Both /vets.html and /vets accept an optional query parameter named specialty; no other request shape carries the filter.
Given /vets.html?specialty=<name> where some veterinarians hold that specialty, only those veterinarians are listed, and paging applies to the narrowed list.
Given /vets?specialty=<name>, the machine-readable document carries only those veterinarians.
Matching is on the whole specialty name, ignoring letter case: radiology, Radiology, and RADIOLOGY all match the seeded radiology specialty.
Matching is not prefix matching: radio matches no veterinarian even though radiology exists.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, the page renders normally with an empty veterinarian list and succeeds (HTTP 200); the machine-readable document carries no veterinarians and succeeds.
Given specialty= or a value of only spaces, both surfaces behave as if the parameter were absent and list every veterinarian, as an empty owner search does (REQ-OWN-002 precedent).
Given a specialty name carrying leading or trailing spaces, both surfaces list what the same name without them lists: ' radiology ' lists the radiology veterinarians (REQ-OWN-002 precedent).
Given no specialty parameter, both surfaces behave exactly as today.
Pagination links on the narrowed page carry the specialty parameter, so following a page link keeps the narrowing in force.
A veterinarian holding several specialties is listed whenever any one of them is named.
No form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the specialty is added to any template (NG-10).
Case-insensitive matching holds on every supported database vendor, not only where the collation happens to ignore case.
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the specialty - NG-10, deferred to its own request
free-text veterinarian search - NG-9 stands, narrowed only to admit this attribute filter
paging the machine-readable list
naming more than one specialty in one request

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Silent-truncation re-examination (the question this round asked): with Distinct present there is no other truncation or disclosure path I can reach. On /vets.html the derived name generates select distinct plus count(distinct ...), so de-duplication happens in SQL before the page-slot budget is applied - the [Leary, Leary] under limit 2 failure mode the implementer witnessed exists only in the Distinct-removed variant, where the drop is silent because Hibernate de-duplicates the fetched list after the limit. On /vets the same predicate runs with Pageable.unpaged(), so no slot budget exists at all. Neither surface reports a truncation, but neither truncates. What the filter does reveal to an unauthenticated caller - which vets hold a given specialty, the match count via totalElements, and whether a name exists at all via empty vs non-empty - is already fully published by the unfiltered /vets and /vets.html responses, which render every vet with its complete specialty list. So no disclosure the filter enables is new information.

Residual, accepted, no fix requested: normalizeSpecialty applies strip() with no length bound or character allowlist, so an arbitrarily long specialty value reaches the JPA bind parameter. It stays a bind parameter (derived query, never string-built JPQL or native SQL), the comparison is lower(specialty.name) = lower(?), and the value's only output sink is a URL-encoded Thymeleaf link-expression parameter - so the reach is one bounded index-less comparison per request on a small table, not injection and not unbounded allocation. Rated LOW on demonstrated reach; a container-level request-parameter size limit already caps the input.

Pre-existing, unchanged by this round, flagged again only so it is not read as newly cleared: /vets.html binds page as a bare int with no lower bound, so page=0 reaches PageRequest.of(-1, 5) and throws IllegalArgumentException. Boot's default error handling does not include the stack trace in the response, so this is an unhandled-500 surface rather than a disclosure. It predates the diff and is untouched by it - the specialty parameter adds no new instance of the class.

Supply chain, carried forward unchanged from round 1: still not run, still not clean. build.gradle is not in the change set at all this round, so no dependency was added or moved, but no NVD match was performed here either - the project configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin and this reviewer has no network access. Still open from round 1 and still outside this diff: findAll(Pageable) remains @Cacheable("vets") with the default key generator, so the caller-supplied page number is a cache key on an unauthenticated route into a cache with neither eviction nor a size bound. system-design Open Question 5 tracks it. findings.description: Verified independently: the build-pass notes' stated reason for dropping to a raw @PersistenceContext EntityManager - that Boot 4 moved TestEntityManager to a spring-boot-jpa-test module 'not on this classpath' - is factually wrong. `./gradlew dependencies --configuration testCompileClasspath` shows spring-boot-jpa-test:4.1.0 IS on the test classpath, pulled in transitively by the already-declared testImplementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-jpa-test' (-> spring-boot-data-jpa-test -> spring-boot-jpa-test). Boot 4 relocated the class to org.springframework.boot.jpa.test.autoconfigure.TestEntityManager (not removed it), and @DataJpaTest - already imported in this file from org.springframework.boot.data.jpa.test.autoconfigure - is meta-annotated with @AutoConfigureTestEntityManager (confirmed via javap on the DataJpaTest.class RuntimeVisibleAnnotations), so an @Autowired TestEntityManager is auto-configured and available for injection exactly as in pre-Boot-4 versions of this file's convention. TestEntityManager.persistAndFlush(E) (confirmed present via javap on the class) is a direct drop-in for the persist()+flush() pair the new test hand-rolls. Using the framework's sanctioned JPA test helper instead of a raw @PersistenceContext EntityManager is the file's established idiom for this kind of setup and should be restored.
